units.text: ⟦0⟧15.1 Options to ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧
units.sourceHTML: 15.1 Options to patch

units.text: Here is a summary of all of the options that GNU ⟦0⟧ accepts. See ⟦1⟧GNU ⟦2⟧ and Traditional ⟦3⟧⟦4⟧, for which of these options are safe to use in older versions of ⟦5⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Here is a summary of all of the options that GNU patch accepts. See GNU patch and Traditional patch, for which of these options are safe to use in older versions of patch.

units.text: Multiple single-letter options that do not take an argument can be combined into a single command line argument with only one dash.
units.sourceHTML: Multiple single-letter options that do not take an argument can be combined into a single command line argument with only one dash.

units.text: Back up the original contents of each file, even if backups would normally not be made. See ⟦0⟧Backup Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Back up the original contents of each file, even if backups would normally not be made. See Backup Files.

units.text: Prepend ⟦0⟧ to backup file names. See ⟦1⟧Backup File Names⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Prepend prefix to backup file names. See Backup File Names.

units.text: Back up the original contents of each file if the patch does not exactly match the file. This is the default behavior when not conforming to POSIX. See ⟦0⟧Backup Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Back up the original contents of each file if the patch does not exactly match the file. This is the default behavior when not conforming to POSIX. See Backup Files.

units.text: Read and write all files in binary mode, except for standard output and ⟦0⟧. This option has no effect on POSIX-conforming systems like GNU/Linux. On systems where this option makes a difference, the patch should be generated by ‘⟦1⟧’. See ⟦2⟧Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Read and write all files in binary mode, except for standard output and /dev/tty. This option has no effect on POSIX-conforming systems like GNU/Linux. On systems where this option makes a difference, the patch should be generated by ‘diff -a --binary’. See Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons.

units.text: Interpret the patch file as a context diff. See ⟦0⟧Selecting the ⟦1⟧ Input Format⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Interpret the patch file as a context diff. See Selecting the patch Input Format.

units.text: Make directory ⟦0⟧ the current directory for interpreting both file names in the patch file, and file names given as arguments to other options. See ⟦1⟧Applying Patches in Other Directories⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Make directory directory the current directory for interpreting both file names in the patch file, and file names given as arguments to other options. See Applying Patches in Other Directories.

units.text: Make merged if-then-else output using ⟦0⟧. See ⟦1⟧Merging Files with If-then-else⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Make merged if-then-else output using name. See Merging Files with If-then-else.

units.text: Print the results of applying the patches without actually changing any files. See ⟦0⟧Predicting what ⟦1⟧ will do⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Print the results of applying the patches without actually changing any files. See Predicting what patch will do.

units.text: Interpret the patch file as an ⟦0⟧ script. See ⟦1⟧Selecting the ⟦2⟧ Input Format⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Interpret the patch file as an ed script. See Selecting the patch Input Format.

units.text: Remove output files that are empty after the patches have been applied. See ⟦0⟧Creating and Removing Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Remove output files that are empty after the patches have been applied. See Creating and Removing Files.

units.text: Assume that the user knows exactly what he or she is doing, and do not ask any questions. See ⟦0⟧Messages and Questions from ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Assume that the user knows exactly what he or she is doing, and do not ask any questions. See Messages and Questions from patch.

units.text: Set the maximum fuzz factor to ⟦0⟧. See ⟦1⟧Helping ⟦2⟧ Find Inexact Matches⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Set the maximum fuzz factor to lines. See Helping patch Find Inexact Matches.

units.text: If ⟦0⟧ is positive, get input files from a revision control system as necessary; if zero, do not get the files; if negative, ask the user whether to get the files. See ⟦1⟧Revision Control⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: If num is positive, get input files from a revision control system as necessary; if zero, do not get the files; if negative, ask the user whether to get the files. See Revision Control.

units.text: Output a summary of usage and then exit.
units.sourceHTML: Output a summary of usage and then exit.

units.text: Read the patch from ⟦0⟧ rather than from standard input. See ⟦1⟧Options to ⟦2⟧⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Read the patch from patchfile rather than from standard input. See Options to patch.

units.text: Let any sequence of blanks (spaces or tabs) in the patch file match any sequence of blanks in the input file. See ⟦0⟧Applying Patches with Changed White Space⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Let any sequence of blanks (spaces or tabs) in the patch file match any sequence of blanks in the input file. See Applying Patches with Changed White Space.

units.text: Interpret the patch file as a normal diff. See ⟦0⟧Selecting the ⟦1⟧ Input Format⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Interpret the patch file as a normal diff. See Selecting the patch Input Format.

units.text: Ignore patches that ⟦0⟧ thinks are reversed or already applied. See also ⟦1⟧. See ⟦2⟧Applying Reversed Patches⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore patches that patch thinks are reversed or already applied. See also -R. See Applying Reversed Patches.

units.text: Do not back up the original contents of files. This is the default behavior when conforming to POSIX. See ⟦0⟧Backup Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Do not back up the original contents of files. This is the default behavior when conforming to POSIX. See Backup Files.

units.text: Use ⟦0⟧ as the output file name. See ⟦1⟧Options to ⟦2⟧⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use file as the output file name. See Options to patch.

units.text: Set the file name strip count to ⟦0⟧. See ⟦1⟧Applying Patches in Other Directories⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Set the file name strip count to number. See Applying Patches in Other Directories.

units.text: Conform to POSIX, as if the ⟦0⟧ environment variable had been set. See ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ and the POSIX Standard⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Conform to POSIX, as if the POSIXLY_CORRECT environment variable had been set. See patch and the POSIX Standard.

units.text: Use style ⟦0⟧ to quote names in diagnostics, as if the ⟦1⟧ environment variable had been set to ⟦2⟧. See ⟦3⟧⟦4⟧ Quoting Style⟦5⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use style word to quote names in diagnostics, as if the QUOTING_STYLE environment variable had been set to word. See patch Quoting Style.

units.text: Use ⟦0⟧ as the reject file name. See ⟦1⟧Reject File Names⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use reject-file as the reject file name. See Reject File Names.

units.text: Assume that this patch was created with the old and new files swapped. See ⟦0⟧Applying Reversed Patches⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Assume that this patch was created with the old and new files swapped. See Applying Reversed Patches.

units.text: Work silently unless an error occurs. See ⟦0⟧Messages and Questions from ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Work silently unless an error occurs. See Messages and Questions from patch.

units.text: Do not ask any questions. See ⟦0⟧Messages and Questions from ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Do not ask any questions. See Messages and Questions from patch.

units.text: Set the modification and access times of patched files from timestamps given in context diff headers, assuming that the context diff headers use local time. See ⟦0⟧Updating Timestamps on Patched Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Set the modification and access times of patched files from timestamps given in context diff headers, assuming that the context diff headers use local time. See Updating Timestamps on Patched Files.

units.text: Interpret the patch file as a unified diff. See ⟦0⟧Selecting the ⟦1⟧ Input Format⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Interpret the patch file as a unified diff. See Selecting the patch Input Format.

units.text: Output version information and then exit.
units.sourceHTML: Output version information and then exit.

units.text: Select the naming convention for backup file names. See ⟦0⟧Backup File Names⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Select the naming convention for backup file names. See Backup File Names.

units.text: Print more diagnostics than usual. See ⟦0⟧Messages and Questions from ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Print more diagnostics than usual. See Messages and Questions from patch.

units.text: Set internal debugging flags. Of interest only to ⟦0⟧ patchers.
units.sourceHTML: Set internal debugging flags. Of interest only to patch patchers.

units.text: Prepend ⟦0⟧ to base names of backup files. See ⟦1⟧Backup File Names⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Prepend prefix to base names of backup files. See Backup File Names.

units.text: Use ⟦0⟧ as the backup extension instead of ‘⟦1⟧’ or ‘⟦2⟧’. See ⟦3⟧Backup File Names⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use suffix as the backup extension instead of ‘.orig’ or ‘~’. See Backup File Names.

units.text: Set the modification and access times of patched files from timestamps given in context diff headers, assuming that the context diff headers use UTC. See ⟦0⟧Updating Timestamps on Patched Files⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Set the modification and access times of patched files from timestamps given in context diff headers, assuming that the context diff headers use UTC. See Updating Timestamps on Patched Files.
